scope: Independent final C5 v2 static ownership/protocol/source and existing actual portable evidence review. No actual Apple SDK, App host or JVM execution.

inventory.note: Source lists are evidence bindings, not Xcode source whitelist. This effective142 is a C5-only static rebind; not S4-composed SDK closure.

ownerAndSuccessConclusions: Actual future producer uses existing public search/detail/paginated TOC, owned BookStore and transferOriginalPreview, actual ChapterFetchManager two-body cache publication, real checked JSON reading position write. No mock HTTP/runtime/store replaces these owners.

Consumer opens existing owned BookStore/reading position files in a distinct App PID, compares persistent identities/variables/position and hashes, then uses the public ChapterFetchManager cache path with sourceResolver count0. It does not prove CoreText/Reader UI layout.

Controller chooses one explicit Simulator for install/container/wrapper/termination, measures data container before and after each host and exact source stamp, and fails if test-without-building changes the container. No assumption that Xcode preserves installation becomes success.

Both raw xcresult summary and tests must prove exactly one qualified passed case with wrapper/export exit0 and no timeout, skip, retry, foreign case or expected failure. Producer pending data alone cannot establish success.

Final v2 waits for actual owned producer exit before exclusive producer marker. Missing PID, registration ESRCH and observed kernel exit each write a bound observation; consumer and final result require it. Synthetic mocked ESRCH vector verifies serialization only, not actual kernel behavior.

Producer claims global cache cleanup only after verifying a fresh UUID has no directory; consumer assigns cleanup UUID only after accepted current producer/control/book/PID validation. Errors can remove fixture-owned data and that authorized UUID only; they never enumerate the default shelf or clear all user caches.

Descriptor/receipt bind current source, nonce, run UUID and real container. Stale namespace/receipt, reused same PID, hash mismatch or incomplete owner publication fail closed. A stale namespace is deliberately not auto-deleted or reused.
Root S4 integration does not alter the four existing C5 baselines; final six-source candidate must still be composed with current S4/control source hashes before any later SDK run.

closedFindings.fix: Consumer ownedID assignment now follows complete accepted producer/control/book/PID validation.
Qualified wrappers pass same --udid as YUEDU_DEST=id=...; retained exact command guard passes.
terminate_producer now precedes producer marker; no false final pass was found in v1, whose final consumer already followed exit.

ProcessLookupError during kernel registration records observation, final result hashes observation. One existing guard errors on a synthetic Windows path fixture then passes after fixture-only path correction; both histories retained.

limits: Actual Apple SDK compilation, install, test-without-building semantics, Simulator container retention, separate App hosts/PIDs, real kqueue and real public cache/position acceptance remain unexecuted (all0). Static Swift parsing and portable mocks cannot approve them.

C5 is a finite synthetic original-source text reader/offline/position chain. It does not establish full source compatibility, user library migration, Reader UI rendering, real device behavior, Apple installation/signing/renewal or profile validity.
No guarantee against malicious concurrent filesystem mutation/PID reuse beyond the explicit fail-closed source/container/path/PID checks; no new global ownership registry is introduced.

Author v1 shadow142 source list belongs to its own C5-only snapshot. v2 explicitly substitutes the two protocol hashes; future root must compose current S4 and final controls rather than reuse an old source stamp.
